source.title: Gene42: Long-Range Genomic Foundation Model With Dense Attention
source.authors: Kirill Vishniakov; Boulbaba Ben Amor; Engin Tekin; Nancy A Elnaker; Karthik Viswanathan; Aleksandr Medvedev; Aahan Singh; Maryam Nadeem; Mohammad Amaan Sayeed; P. Kanithi; Tiago Magalhaes; N. Vassilieva; Dwarikanath Mahapatra; Marco A. F. Pimentel; Shadab Khan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites parameter-count scaling as motivation for training 500M- and 1.1B-parameter models, but does not test the scaling-law claim or fit a scaling relationship.
record.gate_note: The paper reports genomic-model perplexity at different input sequence lengths and context lengths. These measurements do not test power-law scaling with parameter count, training tokens, or compute, nor compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: Gene42 cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation for training 500M and 1.1B models. It fits no scaling law and runs no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute. Perplexity is reported across input sequence and context lengths, and downstream results compare 500M and 1.1B models only incidentally, with no scaling analysis. 'Uses_without_test/T4' overstates the link: the finding is not used as a tool, only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that continuous pretraining extends dense-attention genomic models to 192 kbp and that Gene42 outperforms prior genomic foundation models on benchmarks. They speculate, untested, that larger models could lower long-sequence perplexity.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or fit the original scaling-law method; it evaluates genomic-model perplexity across context lengths.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported perplexity depends on input sequence length and the model’s trained context length; shorter-context models have high perplexity on long sequences, while the 65k and 192k models reach 1.61 at 65 kbp.

fits_no_version.finding: Perplexity depends on input sequence length relative to trained context length: 1.61 at 65 kbp for the 65k and 192k models; 1.78 and 1.85 for the 192k model at 131 kbp and 192 kbp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Genomic LM perplexity depends on evaluation sequence length relative to the trained context length.

record.problems: No parameter, token, or compute scaling sweep or fitted law is reported; no uncertainty estimates are given for the perplexity results.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 includes additional perplexity curves for shorter-context models, but their values are not stated numerically in the text and are not needed to assess a version of the claim.

untested.parts: No loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Genomic modality, but no power-law fit in it.
Two model sizes (500M vs 1.1B) appear in downstream tables, with mixed results, but there is no analysis of scale or loss versus downstream performance.

record.verdict_notes: Downstream tables include 500M vs 1.1B Gene42 models, but training data and context also differ between them. There are only two sizes and no scaling claim, so these are not usable for V6.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or sweep over parameters, training tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or extrapolation to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or fitted parameter/token trends.
No comparison isolating architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study trains on genomic data and reports perplexity, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this modality or another training regime.
No analysis of downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or deviations from fitted power laws.
